title: Learning of the film use and lost royalties
summary: Deke Watson says the song was in a film; Kimball weeps at lost money and talks about copyright renewal.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: But wait, that's not the worst of it. About five years ago, when Deke Watson was down here with the Ink Spots, the groups had changed several times. He told me, in the presence of Walter Pichon, because Walter Pichon introduced me to Deke Watson, he said, there's some of the Ink Spots over there. I said, I don't want to meet them. I said, they're the ones who recorded my number. He said, it isn't their fault. He said, those men were working. Which was true. Yeah, that's right. And he said, come over and meet him. So I went over and talked with him. And Pichon mentioned to him, he said, do you ever remember the number, Don't Let Old Age Creep Up On You? He said, yes. He said, well, that number made ASCAP. He said, it was used in a picture where Cesar Romero and Faye somebody else, I've forgotten who it was, made in 1939 or in 1941. Used it in the movie. He used that picture in the movie. You didn't even know it. I didn't know it. And truthfully, I'm not ashamed to admit it, tears rolled down my face because I knew that I was worth some $50,000 for that.
It should be a good deal. They paid money for that.
And that was something that I lost, regretfully so.
Yeah. Do you know the company? Or I guess too late then to do anything about it? Well, I don't know.
You should have been protected by your copyright. I don't know whether it is still too late. And I may intercede to see whether or not something
can be done. The company is still in business. Must have been one of the major companies.
It changed hands a lot though too, sometimes during the Depression and all that.
But records should be kept of the financing and the remuneration such as it was during
that time. Did you ever renew your copyright? Are you watching that?
No, I haven't renewed it. It's good for 30, 30…

Twenty-six, I think. Twenty-eight years. Twenty-eight? Twenty-eight years and you renew it for another twenty-eight. That's fifty-six. Yeah. Well, it's about time for it to be renewed now. Yeah, the time might be coming up and be worth sharing.
